newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tettamanti takes key stake in Cumnock.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tettamanti takes key stake in Cumnock.

text.p: Swiss investor and industrialist Tito Tettamanti has taken a strategic stake in Cumnock Coal Ltd in the expectation that the small Australian steaming coal producer will again become a takeover target.

The investment by Tettamanti's privately-held Dafen Ltd raised a few industry eyebrows earlier this month as it paid a hefty price for its 9.6 percent stake and its timing coincided with a boardroom tussle and production problems at Cumnock's operations in the Hunter Valley north of Sydney.

Knight said the Tettamanti group did not plan to increase its stake in Cumnock in the near future, and would take a keen interest in the company's annual general meeting to be held in Sydney on Friday afternoon.

Howard, the Cumnock chairman, said earlier this month that the company needed to expand annual coal output beyond the present two million tonnes to survive in an industry that is undergoing rationalisation.
Fellow Hunter Valley miner CIM Resources Ltd began merger talks with Cumnock earlier this year in an attempt to ensure its longevity by achieving greater production.
The talks lapsed when Glencore said it was not interested in a merger -- pushing the Cumnock share price to a low of A$1.60.
Cumnock shares were 20 cents lower at A$2.10 on Friday afternoon in very light trade.
